object_description: elongated base with two transverse upper volumes
design_condition: The building occupies the western part of the plot, with a continuous base along the perimeter and upper volumes set back to open a generous sports and play landscape toward the green corridor.

positive.statement: The arrangement creates a generous open space with sports and play areas toward the green corridor.
The mezzanine floor allows daylight to reach the sports facilities below.
The organization of the schools works well, and the clusters are convincingly designed.
Light-flooded, spacious staircases connect the school floors vertically and are impressive spatially.
The project impresses with its high compactness and space efficiency, with a positive effect on profitability.
The school appears flooded with light and inviting.

negative.statement: The arrangement of the transverse volumes seems somewhat random.
The intentions behind the open-space character and the arbitrary placement of tree volumes remain unclear.
The building is positioned too close to the adjacent path, dissolving the frame of trees.
The mezzanine prevents crossing the building at ground level and creates a hurdle for students with limited mobility.
The cramped stair and access situation on the mezzanine cannot match the quality of the upper floors.
The many roof areas are not used as additional outdoor space or for urban-climatic and ecological purposes.
The proposal cannot fulfill its promise of being a light-filled, open, inviting and inclusive school.
